title.en: Lesson 1. What are you doing right now?

blocks.md:
To describe an action **in progress right now**, take the verb stem and attach **-고 있어요**.

먹다 → 먹 + **고 있어요** → 먹고 있어요 (I am eating)
하다 → 하 + **고 있어요** → 하고 있어요 (I am doing)

There are no vowel harmony changes and no 받침 exceptions. The stem never changes shape.

items.tip: I am eating a meal right now.

blocks.md:
**-아요/-어요 vs. -고 있어요**

- 커피 마셔요: “I drink coffee” (general habit or right now)
- 커피 마시고 있어요: “I am drinking coffee right this second” (cup in hand)

**Past continuous:** attach -고 있었어요 → 자고 있었어요 (I was sleeping).

blocks.q: Which sentence means you are literally in the middle of reading a book right now?
blocks.why: **-고 있어요** marks action currently underway. 읽었어요 is past, 읽을 거예요 is future, and 읽고 싶어요 is a wish.

blocks.meaning: I am waiting for a friend at the bus stop right now.
blocks.why: “지금” (right now) shows the action is underway → **기다리고 있어요**.

blocks.meaning: When you called earlier, I was sleeping.
blocks.why: “아까” sets the past frame; an action in progress in the past uses **-고 있었어요**.

blocks.hint: In-progress action is -고 있어요, using the verb 있다 (to exist/be).
blocks.why: The ending is **-고 있어요**, not -고 이에요.

blocks.q: Translate into Korean: **“I am studying right now.”**  (right now = 지금, to study = 공부하다)
blocks.hint: Start with 지금, then attach -고 있어요 to the stem of 공부하다.
blocks.why: 지금 공부하고 있어요. The stem is 공부하.

blocks.say: 지금 뭐 하고 있어요? 밥 먹고 있어요.
blocks.rom: ji-geum mwo ha-go iss-eo-yo? bap meog-go iss-eo-yo
blocks.q: Say it out loud: “What are you doing right now? I am eating.”

title.en: Lesson 2. Attaching -고 있다 to Any Verb Stem

blocks.md:
**-고 있다** is one of the easiest grammatical patterns in Korean because **the verb stem never changes**.

Whether the stem ends in a vowel or a consonant, has 받침 or irregular letters (like ㄷ or ㅂ), you simply drop **-다** and attach **-고 있어요** directly!
Look at **듣다**! In -아요/-어요, 듣 becomes 들어요 (irregular change). But with -고 있다, the consonant doesn't meet a vowel, so it stays **듣고 있어요** (never 들고 있어요).

items.tip: I am listening to music right now. (듣다 keeps ㄷ → 듣고 있어요)
I am cooking in the kitchen. (요리하다 → 요리하고 있어요)
I am making a gift to send to my friend. (만들다 → 만들고 있어요)

blocks.q: How do you conjugate ‘듣다’ (to listen) with -고 있어요?
blocks.why: -고 attaches directly to the stem without triggering the ㄷ→ㄹ change, so it is **듣고 있어요**. 들고 있어요 means 'holding'.

blocks.q: Match each verb to its continuous -고 있어요 form.

blocks.meaning: I am making coffee in the kitchen right now.
blocks.why: Attach -고 있어요 directly to the stem 만들 → **만들고 있어요**.

blocks.q: Attach -고 있어요 to 쉬다 (to rest): 「지금 집에서 ___ .」
blocks.why: Attach -고 있어요 directly to stem 쉬 → **쉬고 있어요**.

blocks.q: Arrange the words to say: “I am watching television now.”

blocks.say: 방에서 책을 읽고 음악을 듣고 있어요.
blocks.rom: bang-e-seo chaeg-eul ilg-go eum-ag-eul deud-go iss-eo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud: “I am reading a book and listening to music in my room.”

title.ko: 3강. 단순 현재와의 차이와 쓸 수 없는 말
title.en: Lesson 3. Progressive vs. Simple Present & Restrictions

blocks.h: Progressive vs. Simple Present and Adjectives
blocks.md:
How is **-고 있어요** different from the simple polite ending **-아요/-어요**?

- **-아요/-어요:** General habits, states, or actions (e.g., 매일 커피를 마셔요 = I drink coffee every day).
- **-고 있어요:** The action is unfolding right at this exact moment (e.g., 지금 커피를 마시고 있어요 = I am drinking coffee right now).

**CRITICAL RULE:** Adjectives (descriptive words like 크다, 예쁘다, 바쁘다) **CANNOT** use -고 있다! You can never say *예쁘고 있어요 or *바쁘고 있어요.

blocks.md: Clothing verbs like **입다** (to wear) and **신다** (to wear shoes) with -고 있다 mean the state of currently wearing them: **모자를 쓰고 있어요** (I am wearing a hat).

items.tip: I am working at the office right now.

blocks.q: Why is the sentence “날씨가 춥고 있어요” wrong?
options: 춥다 is an adjective and cannot take -고 있다
춥다 needs an irregular ㅂ change before -고
The word 날씨 cannot take the subject particle
blocks.why: Adjectives describe conditions and states, not active physical actions. Only action verbs take -고 있다. The correct sentence is **날씨가 추워요**.

blocks.q: Which sentence naturally means “I am wearing sneakers right now”?
blocks.why: 신다 (to wear on feet) takes -고 있어요 to mean currently wearing: **신고 있어요**.

blocks.q: Match each sentence with its correct nuance.

blocks.meaning: Jimin is wearing a yellow shirt.
blocks.why: 입다 (to wear) + -고 있어요 expresses wearing clothes → **입고 있어요**.

blocks.q: Complete the sentence to say Jimin is wearing a hat: 「지민은 모자를 ___ .」
blocks.why: 쓰다 (to wear on head) takes -고 있어요 → **쓰고 있어요**.

blocks.say: 저는 지금 안경을 쓰고 한국어 책을 읽고 있어요.
blocks.rom: jeo-neun ji-geum an-gyeong-eul sseu-go han-gug-eo chaeg-eul ilg-go iss-eo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud: “I am wearing glasses and reading a Korean book right now.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Real-Life Dialogues: Calls and Appointments

blocks.h: Answering “What are you doing right now?”
blocks.md:
In daily phone calls and text messages, **“지금 뭐 하고 있어요?”** (What are you doing right now?) is one of the most common questions.

Use **-고 있어요** to state your immediate activity, such as being on the move, having a meal, or waiting!
To say you are NOT doing an action right now, say **안 -고 있어요** (e.g., 지금 일 안 하고 있어요 = I'm not working right now).

items.ch: A: 지금 통화할 수 있어요? B: 네, 집에서 쉬고 있어요.
items.tip: A: Can you talk now? B: Yes, I'm resting at home.

items.ch: A: 어디 가요? B: 지하철역으로 걸어가고 있어요.
items.tip: A: Where are you going? B: I'm walking to the subway station.

items.ch: A: 지우 씨 있어요? B: 지금 회의하고 있어요.
items.tip: A: Is Jiu there? B: She is in a meeting right now.

blocks.q: A friend calls and asks: “지금 뭐 하고 있어요?” You are in the middle of preparing lunch. What do you say?
blocks.why: 점심 준비하다 + -고 있어요 becomes **점심 준비하고 있어요**.

blocks.q: You are on the bus heading to meet someone. How do you tell them?
Match each question with its natural continuous response.

blocks.sentence: A: 지금 어디예요? B: 약속 장소로 [가고 있어요].
blocks.meaning: A: Where are you now? B: I am on my way to the meeting place.
blocks.why: 가다 + -고 있어요 → **가고 있어요** (statement form with period).

blocks.q: Reply that you are waiting for a friend: 「카페에서 친구를 ___ .」

blocks.say: 미안해요, 지금 지하철을 타고 가고 있어서 나중에 전화할게요.
blocks.rom: mi-an-hae-yo, ji-geum ji-ha-cheol-eul ta-go ga-go iss-eo-seo na-jung-e jeon-hwa-hal-ge-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud: “Sorry, I am taking the subway right now so I will call you later.”
